prompts.title: High-Contrast Monochrome Portrait Prompt
prompts.prompt: Create a striking, ultra-detailed, high-contrast monochrome lack-and-white) portrait based on the uploaded reference image. The subject’s facial structure and identity must match the reference precisely accurately replicate bone structure, eye shape, nose proportions, jawline definition, beard density (if present), hairline, and overall facial symmetry. Maintain authentic skin texture and natural features without artificial smoothing. Subject & Expression A mature, confident man with a strong facial structure and deep-set eyes looking directly into the camera. Expression should be serious, contemplative, and quietly authoritative. Preserve natural skin details such as pores, fine lines, and subtle texture for realism. The gaze should feel focused and introspective, not aggressive. Facial Hair (Adaptive) If facial hair is present in the reference image, replicate it exactly — density, length, shape, and edges. Maintain natural tonal variation (including salt-and-pepper graying if applicable). Beard lines should be clean and structured. If clean-shaven, preserve realistic skin texture and jaw definition. Hairstyle (Adaptive) Match the hairstyle from the reference image exactly — volume, direction, hairline, and texture. Hair should look natural with visible strand detail and subtle specular highlights from overhead directional lighting. Pose Classic “thinker” pose. One hand raised to the chin with thumb along the jawline and index finger slightly curled. Knuckles and tendons subtly defined for realism. Hand in sharp focus with visible skin texture and natural tonal gradation. 🔥 Lighting & Technical Style (Accurately Customized) Low-key fine-art studio photography with controlled high-contrast sculpting. • Primary key light positioned slightly above eye level and slightly toward the viewer’s left, angled downward to create strong top-plane highlights. • Light is soft but directional (large softbox or diffused beauty dish), producing crisp edge definition without harsh clipping. • Strong highlight concentration on forehead center, nose bridge, upper cheekbones, beard texture, and the top planes of the hand. • Subtle shadow shaping under the brow ridge and cheekbones to enhance bone structure. • The shadow side of the face remains deep but not fully crushed — maintaining controlled midtone detail. • Minimal fill light from front-center to retain facial symmetry while preserving depth. • Very subtle rim separation along hair edges and outer shoulder to prevent blending into background. • Catchlights centered and natural — small, soft rectangular reflection in both eyes. • Background is fully black with zero visible texture, absorbing all spill light. Contrast ratio should be high but refined — not blown highlights, not muddy blacks. Clean tonal roll-off. Composition Tight vertical head-and-shoulders crop (portrait orientation, 4:5 ratio recommended). Subject centered symmetrically for a formal, balan
prompts.description: An extremely detailed prompt for generating a high-contrast, black-and-white fine-art studio portrait, requiring precise replication of the subject's identity, facial features, and expression from a reference image. It specifies complex lighting setup (low-key, directional softbox) and composition (tight vertical crop, 'thinker' pose).

prompts.title: Intimate Cinematic Couple Portrait
prompts.prompt: Use the exact same faces from both reference images and generate a warm intimate cinematic couple portrait where both faces emerge from soft darkness radiating pure joy and happiness. Two faces close together — cheek almost to cheek, heads tilted naturally toward each other, the man slightly behind and to the side of the woman. Both wearing the most genuine natural smiles — not posed, not magazine perfect — real, alive, the kind of smile that happens when you are completely happy with exactly who you are with. Eyes crinkled at the corners with real laughter, teeth naturally showing, the specific warmth of two people who are genuinely crazy about each other. The woman's smile bright and glowing, the man's carrying that quiet proud happiness of someone who cannot believe how lucky they are. Only the faces visible — everything below the chin dissolved completely into warm darkness. No shoulders, no clothing, no hands — just two glowing happy faces floating together in the dark like the only two people in the universe. Lighting is a {argument name="lighting" default="single warm golden source"} from slightly above and between them — soft, intimate, wrapping both faces in the same rich amber glow simultaneously. The light feels like candlelight or a warm lamp — alive and human. Cheekbones and nose tips catching the brightest warmth, the smiles fully illuminated, eyes sparkling with natural catch lights. Both faces fading gradually into warm darkness at the edges — soft and beautiful. Background is pure warm black void — no texture, no location, just darkness that feels safe and intimate rather than cold or dramatic. Color grading is warm, golden and joyful — rich ambers, honey tones, glowing skin, the palette of happiness itself. 6% film grain for analog warmth. Slight halation glow around the brightest highlights. Both faces equally sharp and present. Shot on simulated {argument name="camera" default="Leica Noctilux 50mm f/0.95"}. The "OzairAI" watermark dissolved invisibly into the lower-right darkness. Vertical 9:13 format. Ultra photorealistic, 8K — two faces, one light, infinite happiness.
prompts.description: A high-detail prompt for creating a warm, intimate portrait of a couple using reference images for facial consistency.

prompts.title: Watchmaker's Documentation Board (Exploded View)
prompts.prompt: A master watchmaker's documentation board for {argument name="timepiece" default="a Tourbillon Chronograph"} — {argument name="manufacture" default="Patek Philippe"} / {argument name="complication" default="Perpetual Calendar"} / {argument name="year" default="1950"}. Left section: historical context showing the original patent drawings, period advertisements in gilded frames, and archival photographs of the atelier with craftsmen at work. Center section: the movement in exploded view, every wheel, spring, and jewel suspended in precise spatial relationship, with material callouts (Geneva stripes, blued screws, ruby bearings) and functional annotations tracing the flow of power from mainspring to escapement. Right section: the completed watch in its defining context—wrist of an explorer, pocket of a diplomat, or display case of a collector—captured with shallow depth and warm side lighting. Visual style transitions from sepia patent office to mechanical precision chrome to intimate portraiture. Title block reading "{argument name="watch name" default="[WATCH NAME]"} — CALIBRE {argument name="calibre number" default="[NUMBER]"}, {argument name="complication" default="[COMPLICATION]"}, CIRCA {argument name="year" default="[YEAR]"}".
prompts.description: A prompt template designed to generate a complex, multi-section documentation board for a timepiece, blending historical patent drawings, a detailed exploded view of the movement (with material callouts), and an intimate portrait of the completed watch, transitioning visual styles across the board.

prompts.title: Winter Solstice City Food Art Poster Prompt
prompts.prompt: A city rendering digital art poster for 【{argument name="city name" default="city name"}】, with the Winter Solstice solar term as the overall background atmosphere. The core subject of the image is a floating miniature island, shaped like the selected city and occupying most of the frame. The outline of the island is similar to the city's map shape, seamlessly integrating the city's unique iconic landmarks, natural landscapes, and cultural elements. The miniature island is entirely carried or enveloped by the most representative traditional food imagery of the city during the Winter Solstice. Only one specific type of food should be chosen, determined by the city and regional culture (e.g., dumplings, tangyuan). Do not show a specific plate, but translate the form, texture, and structure of this oversized food into the island's shell, terrain, or supporting structure, making the city appear to grow upon this large Winter Solstice food item. The island is placed within a realistic yet restrained Winter Solstice cooking scene based on the traditional food mentioned above, such as a stove, boiling pot/steamer, or soup pot in a daily kitchen environment. However, background elements are presented with blurring and soft focus, only hinting at the atmosphere of life and cooking. Steam and heat slowly rise, combining with warm winter lighting to create a quiet, warm, and human-touch solar term atmosphere. Cinematic lighting, vibrant but restrained colors, aerial perspective, and winter light reflection effects. The number of buildings should not be too many or too dense. The interior of the island showcases a seamless blend of history and modernity: one part presents the city's most representative ancient historical buildings; the other part naturally transitions into the city's landmark buildings and skyline view, all reflecting the current weather conditions (must confirm real weather conditions). 3D text of the city's Chinese name, formed by the steam from the pot, floats above the miniature island. The text acts like a miniature ecological device coexisting with the Winter Solstice, food, and city culture. Around the frame and the main subject, add an information layout layer with a Winter Solstice festive atmosphere and local life feel, with the overall style conforming to traditional Chinese culture. Automatically retrieve basic city information and Winter Solstice solar term information related to 【city name】, providing a simple introduction. Text layout uses an asymmetrical, naturally distributed arrangement, scattered around the edges and negative space of the frame, avoiding strict grids and centered composition. In the corners or edges of the frame, present the city's geographical coordinates, alias, or founding year, and the weather and solar term reminder for the Winter Solstice day, in the style of a local festival poster or old calendar, as decorative information elements. The overall layout maintains significant negative space, but the atmosphere leans towards warmth, domesticity, and festivity. The copywriting should be concise and refined. Style requirements: Octane Render, C4D, Isometric City, Micro World, Living Ecosystem, 8k Resolution, DreamWorks style, 3D modeling, delicate, soft light projection Size: Vertical 9:16
prompts.description: A modified version of the City Poster prompt (tweet 2002592082125578427) specifically tailored for the Winter Solstice festival. The miniature city island is now carried or enveloped by a giant representation of the city's most traditional Winter Solstice food (like dumplings or tangyuan). The scene is set in a warm, domestic kitchen environment with steam and soft lighting, emphasizing a festive, traditional Chinese cultural style.

prompts.title: Isometric 3D Diorama of Product Evolution Prompt
prompts.prompt: Input Variable: {argument name="topic" default="[INSERT TOPIC]"} (e.g., The History of Bread, The Making of Whiskey, The Story of Silk, The Evolution of Paper) System Instruction: Generate a hyper-realistic, isometric 3D diorama displayed on an unrolled antique map. Use the following logic to procedurally generate the scene: 1. Deconstruction: Analyze the Input: Break the topic into 3 Phases of Production (From Nature to Consumption). The Material Path: Identify the raw unit of the topic (e.g., Coffee Beans, Wheat Grains, Silk Cocoons, Wood Chips). This material will form the physical "Road" connecting the scenes. 2. Container (The Chart): The Object: A large, textured Parchment Scroll with curled edges, unrolled on a rich Mahogany wooden table. The Layout: An "S-Curve" Path winds through the center of the scroll, connecting three distinct raised platforms. The Timeline: Delicate black ink timeline markers (dates like 1600, 1850, 1920) run alongside the path. 3. Vignettes (The Production Line): CRITICAL: Do not generate Sci-Fi. Stick to Historic and Modern Classic aesthetics. Top Left - The Source): Concept: The Agricultural or Raw Origin. Visuals: Rows of crops, a mine, or a forest growing directly out of a wooden block base. Figures: Tiny farmers or laborers in period-appropriate rustic clothing harvesting the raw material. Top Right - The Industry): Concept: The Processing and Refinement (Industrial Revolution Era). Visuals: A factory or mill with Copper Stills, Brass Gears, Smokestacks, or Water Wheels . Figures: Workers operating machinery, steam rising from vents. Bottom Left - The Experience): Concept: The Final Consumption (The "Golden Age"). Visuals: A warm, inviting interior. A Victorian Pub, a Parisian Cafe, a Tailor Shop, or a Library. Figures: Patrons enjoying the finished product in a social setting. 4. The "Hero" Object (Bottom Right): Instead of a fourth building, the path ends at a Life-Sized "Hero" Object sitting on the paper. (e.g., A perfect porcelain Cup of Coffee, A Loaf of Sourdough, A Crystal Whiskey Tumbler). 5. Visual Syntax: The Path: The road connecting the buildings is NOT dirt or asphalt. It is a River of the Raw Material (e.g., A road paved with Coffee Beans or Wheat grains). Typography: An elegant Serif Header at the bottom: "The Evolution of [Input]". Lighting: Warm, indoor "Library" lighting. Soft shadows, rich wood tones, no harsh neons. Output: ONE image, 1:1 Aspect Ratio, Isometric Diorama, "Anno 1800" Strategy Game Aesthetic, High Texture,
prompts.description: A complex, multi-step system instruction prompt designed to generate a hyper-realistic, isometric 3D diorama illustrating the evolution of a product (like bread or whiskey) across three phases (Source, Industry, Experience). The diorama is displayed on an unrolled antique map, with the path connecting the scenes made of the raw material itself, simulating an 'Anno 1800' strategy game aesthetic.

prompts.title: Encyclopedia of Flavor Diorama Generator
prompts.prompt: Input Variable: [{argument name="cuisine or dish" default="INSERT CUISINE OR DISH"}] (e.g., Persian Kebabs, Japanese Sushi, Italian Pasta, Mexican Tacos) System Instruction: Generate a hyper-realistic, wide-angle (16:9) 3D diorama of an "Encyclopedia of Flavor." Use the following logic to procedurally generate the scene: 1. Flavor Profiling: Analyze the Input: Determine the Region , Staple Ingredients , and Cooking Method . (e.g., Kebab = Fire/Coal, Rice, Meat. Sushi = Water, Fish, Rice). The Terrain: The pages of the book must physically transform into the landscape of the cuisine. Grain: Rice or Couscous forms dunes. Liquid: Sauces or Broths form rivers. Solid: Bread or Meat forms mountains/cliffs. 2. Container (The Wide Atlas): The Object: A massive, horizontal Landscape-Format Atlas lying open on an aged wooden banquet table. The Spine: Runs horizontally through the center, acting as the "Equator" or "Main Road" of the scene. The Paper: Parchment texture. The edges of the pages are tattered and stained with spices (Saffron, Paprika, Turmeric). 3. Panoramic Composition (Left to Right Flow): CRITICAL: Do not place distinct plates. Create a continuous flow across the open spread. Left Side (The Origin - Agriculture): The raw ingredients grow out of the paper. (e.g., Wheat stalks rising from the text; Cattle grazing on parsley fields; Fishermen casting nets into ink-blue water). Center (The Process - The Kitchen): The spine is the cooking zone. (e.g., A miniature Tandoor oven or Grill built into the book binding; Steam rising volumetrically). Right Side (The Result - The Feast): The finished dish explodes in scale. (e.g., A mountain of Saffron Rice topped with the Kebab; A Ziggurat of Sushi). 4. The Micro-Population The Figures: 1:87 Scale (HO Scale) figures populate the landscape. The Action: They are working the food. Harvesting: Picking herbs from the margins. Transporting: Carrying giant peppercorns like boulders. Cooking: Using flamethrowers to char the meat or rakes to fluff the rice. 5. Lighting & Atmosphere: Aspect Ratio: 16:9 Horizontal. Lighting: "Golden Hour" side-lighting. It should skim across the texture of the food and the paper grain, emphasizing the "Landscape" feel. Steam: Volumetric steam connects the three zones (Left, Center, Right). Output: ONE image, 16:9 Aspect Ratio, Macro Diorama Photography, Octane Render, High Texture Fidelity.
prompts.description: A highly complex, multi-step instructional prompt for generating a wide-angle 3D diorama of an 'Encyclopedia of Flavor' based on a cuisine input. The prompt requires the AI to procedurally transform the pages of an open atlas into a landscape made of food ingredients (rice dunes, sauce rivers), populated by miniature working figures (HO Scale), all rendered with Octane Render and Golden Hour lighting.

prompts.title: NES BG Dot Art Conversion Prompt
prompts.prompt: [NES Final Specification/Complete Version: BG-Only Algorithm Execution Type Dot Art Conversion Prompt] Convert this image into BG dot art specifications for the Family Computer (NES) hardware, strictly executing the following mathematical and logical steps, without limiting the subject matter. The purpose of this prompt is to satisfy the constraints required for BG to function on actual NES hardware. Aesthetic-only NES-style expression is prohibited. Use only the BG layer; sprites are strictly prohibited. ──────────────────────── [Prerequisites (NES BG Implementation Rules)] ──────────────────────── - Output Resolution: 256 × 240 pixels - Layer Used: NES BG only - Sprite usage prohibited - Transparency processing is not performed - Index 0 of each palette is treated as the NES universal background color - Index 0 is common to all palettes - The color with the largest coverage area on the entire screen is assigned as the universal background color - Color number 0 can also be used as a normal drawing color ──────────────────────── [Step 1: Geometric Image Processing (Protagonist Priority, No Deformation Cropping)] ──────────────────────── 1. Set the conversion size to 256 × 240 pixels 2. Always maintain the aspect ratio of the original image - Scale up or down until the shorter side fits the conversion size - Stretching the image is strictly prohibited 3. Automatically detect the protagonist (person, animal, building, etc.) in the image, and adjust the crop position so that the protagonist is maximally contained within the frame 4. If the protagonist cannot be detected, crop based on the center of the screen ──────────────────────── [Step 2: Tile Decomposition and Attribute Block Definition (NES Compliant)] ──────────────────────── 1. Divide the image into 8×8 pixel tiles 2. Treat 2×2 tiles (16×16 pixels) as 1 attribute block 3. Subsequent palette constraints and color constraints must be applied per attribute block ──────────────────────── [Step 3: Attribute Block Unit Palette Clustering (Maximum 4)] ──────────────────────── 1. Analyze the color distribution within each 16×16 attribute block 2. Cluster all attribute blocks by color distribution similarity, classifying them into a maximum of 4 groups 3. If the hue (blue, green, etc.) is clearly different from other areas, treat it as an independent group whenever possible 4. However, the NES BG sub-palettes are limited to a maximum of 4. Prioritize the protagonist area, and areas of low importance may be integrated into similar colors ──────────────────────── [Step 4: NES BG Palette Generation (4 colors × 4 sets)] ──────────────────────── 1. Index 0 (Universal Background Color) - Calculate the color with the largest coverage area on the entire screen, and assign it to Index 0, common to all palettes 2. Index 1–3 (Unique Colors) - For each sub-palette, select 3 colors that represent the 'light part,' 'mid-tone,' and 'dark part' of that attribute group - Colors extremely close in hue or brightness to Index 0 are prohibited ──────────────────────── [NES Color Palette Constraints (Hardware Compliant, NTSC)] ──────────────────────── - Available colors are strictly limited to the 54 NES hardware-compliant NTSC palette colors listed below - Palette generation, color selection, and quantization must always be performed from this 54-color set - Generation of new colors, RGB interpolation, or use of continuous values is prohibited - The following color set contains exactly 54 colors NES NTSC usable palette (54 colors, hex RGB) 000000,1D2B53,7E2553,#008751,AB5236,5F574F, C2C3C7,FFF1E8,FF004D,FFA300,FFEC27,00E436, 29ADFF,83769C,FF77A8,FFCCAA,291814,111D35, 422136,125359,742F29,49333B,A28879,F3EF7D, BE2633,E06F8B,E0A872,B2DCEF,4F6781,8E478C, A3CE27,44891A,2A4F3E,6D758D,9D9D9D,FFFFFF, 4B692F,6A6A6A,8F563B,C2C3C7,DF7126,D95763, D77BBA,FBF236,99E550,6ABE30,37946E,5FCDE4, CBDBFC,ADB5BD,EEC39A,696A6A ──────────────────────── [Step 5: CHR Pattern Compression (BG 256 Tile Limit)] ──────────────────────── 1. Calculate the number of unique 8×8 tile patterns used across the entire image 2. Limit the number of unique tiles to not exceed 256 types 3. For large areas like backgrounds, sky, or walls, repeatedly use completely identical dot patterns to minimize the number of tile types 4. Tiles with slight differences may be integrated using the following methods: - Readjustment of dither placement - Replacement of intermediate colors - Requantization within the attribute block ──────────────────────── [Step 6: Dithering (NES 4-Color Constraint Support)] ──────────────────────── 1. Use only the 4 assigned colors within each attribute block 2. To express pseudo-gradation, apply the following dither
prompts.description: An extremely detailed, multi-step LLM prompt designed to convert any image into a background (BG) dot art image strictly adhering to the technical specifications and constraints of the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) hardware, including resolution, color palettes, tile limits, and dithering techniques. This prompt was originally developed for Gemini's Nano Banana Pro but was later used to build a dedicated tool due to LLM interpretation issues.

This soft lighting creates gradual gray shadows that naturally shape the right side of his face, pool in the deep folds of his black jacket, and gently fall across the right side of the background, establishing a balanced, analogous palette of warm brown neutrals anchored by heavy rich blacks. Captured with the cinematic polish of modern commercial menswear editorial digital photography, shot straight-on using an 85mm lens at f/2.8, 1/200s, and ISO 400 to achieve a medium depth of field that isolates the tack-sharp subject against the softly recognizable architectural background without digital grain, featuring a warm color balance, a subtle contrast curve that preserves rich black tones, and gentle skin retouching, entirely framed in a 9:16 aspect ratio.

The Stage: An L-Shaped Display Box (Vertical Backboard + Horizontal Floor). The Finish: Clean, matte Cream or White plastic, resembling a high-end educational kit or museum exhibit. The Frame: A simple wooden or plastic border framing the scene. 3. Periodic Table background: The Grid: The vertical wall features a neat, symmetrical grid of circular Petri Dishes or Ceramic Bowls . The Contents: Each dish contains a sample of the "States of Matter" (Step 1). The Swatches: Below the dishes are square tiles displaying the "Texture Samples" (e.g., a square of perfectly tempered chocolate next to a bloomed one). The Labels: Tiny, legible scientific text (Serif font) printed directly on the wall under each sample. 4. The Floor (The Laboratory): The Narrative: A 1:12 scale Scientist or Chef figure (wearing a lab coat) stands at a central wooden workbench. Equipment: The desk is cluttered with a mix of Chemistry Glassware (Beakers, Flasks) and Culinary Tools (Whisks, Scales). The Experiment: The figure is actively testing or measuring the food product. 5. Typography : Placement: Massive, thick 3D Extruded Letters stand on the very front edge of the floor, acting as a barrier. Construction: The letters are made of the food itself (e.g., "THE CHEMISTRY OF CHOCOLATE" molded in dark chocolate). Text: "THE CHEMISTRY OF {argument name="Input A" default="CHOCOLATE"}". Output: ONE image, 1:1 Aspect Ratio, Studio Product Lighting, "Wes Anderson" Symmetry, Educational Aesthetic.

prompts.title: 2x2 Grid Product Invention Visualization (Patent/Marketing)
prompts.prompt: Input Variable: {argument name="input objects" default="[INSERT 1 or 2 OBJECTS]"} Instruction: Act as a Visionary Industrial Designer and Patent Clerk. Create a 2x2 Grid visualizing the invention of a new product based on the Input. Innovation Logic : Analyze Functions: Identify the primary utility of Input A and Input B. The Fusion: Combine them into a single, cohesive device that solves a specific (niche) problem. If 2 Inputs: Hybridize them (e.g., Mug + Grater = A self-cooling mug with a garnish shaver). If 1 Input: Evolve it (e.g., Toothbrush = A self-sanitizing, toothpaste-injecting smart wand). The Branding: Generate a catchy, corporate product name (e.g., "The Breeze-Grate™", "Solar-Brella Pro"). The Visual Structure (The 2x2 Grid): CRITICAL: The image must be split into 4 distinct quadrants with different visual styles. Panel 1 (Top Left): The Exploded Patent View Style: Black & White Technical Line Art. Thin distinct lines, no shading. Content: An isometric "Exploded View" of the device, showing the internal motor, battery, or mechanism separated from the shell. Detail: Add Numbered Leader Lines (10, 12, 14) pointing to specific parts. Panel 2 (Top Right): The Functional Diagram Style: Black & White Schematic with bold arrows. Content: A cross-section or "In-Use" drawing showing how how the device works. Use Action Arrows to show airflow, rotation, or liquid movement. Detail: Show the "Result" (e.g., cheese falling, water spraying). Panel 3 (Bottom Left): The Product Render Style: High-End Studio Photography. Color, Glossy, "Apple/Braun" Design Aesthetic. Content: The final physical product sitting on a white reflective surface. It should look sleek, using materials like White Ceramic, Brushed Aluminum, or Matte Plastic. Context: Include a small prop to show scale (e.g., a block of cheese, a coffee bean, a hand). Panel 4 (Bottom Right): The Marketing Pitch Style: Editorial Magazine Layout. White background, black text. Typography: Headline: Large, Bold Serif Text displaying the [Invention Name]. Body: A block of clean "Lorem Ipsum" or readable text describing the "Revolutionary Features." Bullets: A small list of specs (e.g., "Dishwasher Safe," "USB-C"). Visual Syntax: Cohesion: The product design in Panel 3 must perfectly match the line art in Panel 1. Design Language: Minimalist, Ergonomic, Consumer Electronics aesthetic. Even if the idea is silly, the design must look expensive. Output: 2x2 Grid, Mixed Media (Line Art vs. Photorealism), 8k Resolution, "Kickstarter Campaign" Aesthetic.
prompts.description: A complex, multi-panel prompt designed to visualize the invention and marketing of a new product by combining two concepts (or evolving one). It mandates a 2x2 grid structure, with each quadrant requiring a distinct visual style: technical line art (Exploded Patent View), schematic diagram (Functional Diagram), photorealistic render (Product Render), and editorial layout (Marketing Pitch). The prompt acts as an industrial designer, focusing on cohesion between the panels and a minimalist, consumer electronics aesthetic.

prompts.prompt: A cinematic speed-motion shot of the uploaded reference character captured mid-slide on a rain-slicked, neon-drenched cyberpunk street. The focus is equally on the reflection and the character, forming a dual-layer composition. Likeness Preservation (CRITICAL): Maintain exact proportions, eye shape, spacing, stylization, silhouette, and material identity from the reference. Do not humanize. Do not reinterpret anatomy. Do not modify facial structure. Identity must remain perfectly intact and instantly recognizable. 2D to 3D Translation (ONLY if input is 2D artwork): If the uploaded reference is 2D (illustration, anime, flat graphic, cel-shaded), convert it into a fully realized 3D cinematic form while preserving exact identity fidelity. Maintain exact head shape, eye design, spacing, and proportions. Preserve original stylization, do NOT add realism that alters design language. Translate linework into subtle surface geometry or shading transitions. Keep original colors, expressed through physically believable materials. Convert flat shading into controlled cinematic light falloff. The result must feel physically real, not redesigned. Camera & Perspective: Ultra-low angle, camera positioned just centimeters above the wet pavement. Lens: 18–20mm ultra-wide. Slight Dutch tilt (5–10 degrees) to destabilize the frame. Front three-quarter perspective. One limb or body part must be closer to the lens, creating perspective pressure. Composition (Reflection Dominance): The character slices diagonally across the upper half of the frame. The lower half is dominated by a sharp but slightly distorted reflection. Vertical neon signs in the background must mirror into the wet ground, forming strong graphic lines. The composition must feel off-balance and tension-driven, not centered or stable. Pose Enforcement (CRITICAL — OVERRIDE ALL DEFAULT STANCES): The character must NOT be upright, balanced, or casually sliding. The pose must represent loss of balance under high speed. The torso is pitched aggressively forward, close to the ground. One limb forcefully contacts the wet surface, creating splash and friction. The opposite limb extends outward or backward, fully stretched for counterbalance. Legs are asymmetrical: one trailing, one collapsing or stepping incorrectly. Spine forms a diagonal or curved line, never vertical. Head leads the motion slightly ahead of the torso. Weight Distribution: Weight is NOT centered. It collapses toward the contacting limb and forward motion. Ground Interaction (MANDATORY): Water splashes outward from impact points. Friction streaks beneath sliding limb. Surface tension visibly disturbed. Energy Read: The pose must feel like mid-fall recovery, evasive maneuver at high speed, barely controlled momentum. NOT clean skating, surfing, balanced glide, or upright slide. Perspective Amplification: At least one limb must appear larger due to proximity to the lens, enhancing speed and aggression. Motion & Blur: Directional motion blur trailing from the lowest moving limbs. Sharp focal plane on the face or upper torso. Background and trailing limbs fall into controlled blur. Lighting & Color (Cyberpunk Neon): Hard directional neon lighting from off-screen vertical sources. Color palette: deep cyan, magenta, electric yellow. Lighting behavior: sharp highlights on wet surfaces, strong rim light separating silhouette, deep shadow pockets. No flat lighting. Surface Detail (Hyper-Reflective): Wet pavement must feel physically real: mirror-like reflections with ripple distortion, micro scratches and pooling water, subtle rain impact patterns. Character materials slightly darkened from moisture. Atmosphere: Heavy rain and mist in the background. Volumetric light beams cutting through haze. Dense air perspective. Foreground may include subtle water droplets or mist near lens for depth. Emotion: Urgency. Instability. High-stakes motion. The character is either escaping or chasing. Negative Constraints: No centered composition. No upright balanced pose. No clean symmetrical stance. No dry surfaces. No flat reflections. No studio lighting. No evenly sharp full-frame clarity. No static posture. Background Pixel Wall Art (Depth-Controlled): Replace the LED sign with a weathered wall-mounted pixel-art mural or printed panel of the character. The pixel version must preserve silhouette and identity but appear faded, worn, and partially damaged. Printed or painted on a rough wall surface, not glowing like a screen. Subtle grime, scratches, peeling, or moisture distortion. Colors desaturated and affected by environment. Depth Control (CRITICAL): Must sit clearly in the background plane. Slightly obscured by haze, rain, or foreground motion. Edges softened, not crisp. Reduced contrast compared to main subject. Lighting Integration: Does NOT emit light. Only receives ambient neon spill. Partially falls into shadow. Pixel Art Identity Lock (CRITICAL): The pixel-art version must be a direct downscaled translation of the original character, not a reinterpretation. Preserve exact silhouette, head shape, and proportions. Preserve exact eye shape and spacing in simplified pixel form. Use the same facial structure logic — do NOT invent or add features. STRICT PROHIBITIONS: No added nose. No added mouth. No added facial features that do not exist in the original. No stylization drift toward generic pixel characters. If the original character has a minimal or abstract face, the pixel version must remain equally minimal. Foreground Chaos Layer (CRITICAL – DEPTH & IMMERSION): Introduce aggressive near-lens elements that partially obstruct the frame and enhance depth. Near-Lens Elements: Water droplets, splashes, or streaks crossing very close to the camera. Out-of-focus rain particles catching neon light. Small debris or mist fragments passing across the lens plane. These elements must feel physically between the viewer and the character, not part of the background. Depth Behavior (MANDATORY): Foreground elements are heavily out of focus due to proximity. Large soft bokeh shapes or streaks may partially cover edges of the frame. Some elements may briefly occlude parts of the character or reflection. The frame must feel layered: foreground chaos, main subject, background environment. prompts.title: World-in-a-Box Cutaway Diorama Prompt
prompts.prompt: role: You are a cutaway diorama builder and practical-effects set designer. Convert any topic into a “world-in-a-box” cutaway model that reveals internal layers and cause-and-effect using tiny agents, mechanical pathways, and labeled physical artifacts (no holograms, no bioluminescent vibes). logic: Identify the system boundary and 4–7 internal layers (inputs → processing → storage → decisions → outputs → feedback → failure modes). Build a boxed cross-section where each layer is a “floor” with physical machinery appropriate to the topic: conveyors, pipes, filing cabinets, gears, switchboards, kitchens, factories, archives, workshops. Show flow with tangible cues: string lines, arrows painted on wood, marbles in tracks, paper slips moving through slots, stamped tokens traveling between stations. Populate with toyified miniature workers/agents representing roles in the system (analyst, inspector, builder, messenger, operator) interacting with stations. Include one authority signal as a physical document pinned inside the box (audit report, signed approval, certification card, official notice). Add one small “failure corner” (jammed conveyor, leaking pipe, broken bridge) and one “fix corner” (reinforced part, upgraded tool, labeled improvement) to teach contrast. Compose for clarity: 3/4 view, strong leading lines, readable layers, tactile materials, subtle labels. Output: Draw Image (a) a single hero scene (boxed cutaway on a desk), (b) 5 layer/prop callouts with what they symbolize, (c) camera + lighting notes (soft practical lighting, gentle shadows for depth), (d) optional negative cues (avoid abstract fog, avoid neon, avoid chaotic clutter). Everything must be inferred from the topic. no texts
prompts.description: A complex, instruction-based prompt designed to convert any topic (e.g., Bleach) into a highly detailed, physical 'world-in-a-box' cutaway diorama. It requires the model to act as a set designer, identifying internal layers (inputs, processing, failure modes) and representing them with physical machinery, tiny agents (miniature workers), and tangible flow cues (strings, marbles), avoiding abstract or digital aesthetics.

Please fill in according to the following logic: **"An exquisite 3D Isometric Miniature Diorama, solid color background.** **1. Visual Anchor:** The main subject of the scene is a miniature version of **[VAR_PRODUCT]**, with the company's 3D Logo on top of the structure. **2. Stage 3 (Industrial): The Butcher/Baker (Dirty White Apron, Cleaver, Rolled Sleeves). Stage 4 (Ancient): The Hunter/Gatherer (Tunic, Loincloth, Stone Tools, Fire). 2. The Composition : Perspective: High Angle (75 Degrees). Not completely flat. We need to see the bodies of the tiny figures, not just their heads. The Orbits: 5 Distinct Concentric Rings. The Boundary (The Catwalk): Between each ring, there is a visible Negative Space (a thin gap). This is where the tiny chefs stand, presenting the food to the viewer. 3. The Rings & The Residents Logic): The Center (Modern Pinnacle): Food: Deconstructed, gourmet plating on slate. The Figure: A Master Chef carefully placing a micro-green garnish with tweezers. Ring 1 (The Commercial Age): Food: Bright packaging, uniformity. The Figure: A Teenage Fast Food Worker holding a tray or a soda cup, standing next to the cardboard boxes. Ring 2 (The Domestic Age): Food: Casserole dishes or patterned china. The Figure: A 1950s Housewife or Home Cook holding a serving spoon or pie cutter. Ring 3 (The Industrial Age): Food: Cast iron skillets, tin plates, hearty portions. The Figure: A burly 19th Century Butcher or Cook holding a heavy knife or iron ladle. Ring 4 (The Ancient Origin): Food: Cooking over open fire, stone tools, raw ingredients (but cooked/charred enough to look appetizing). prompts.title: Visual Infographic of Ancient Chinese Official Ranks and Attire
prompts.prompt: Create a historical diagram-style infographic, 16:9 horizontal composition, titled "Visual Deconstruction of the Ancient Chinese Official Attire Ranking System." Adopt the aesthetic of ancient canonical diagrams and draw in the style of illustrations from ancient books. The image should display a comparison of the official uniforms of nine ranks of officials from the {argument name="dynasty" default="Qing Dynasty"}, arranged from left to right by rank: nine standing figures from the first to the ninth rank. Above each figure, use fine-line painting (Gongbi) to label the "Buzi (Rank Badge) Pattern" (First Rank Crane, Second Rank Golden Pheasant, Third Rank Peacock... Ninth Rank Quail; civil officials use flying birds, military officials use fierce beasts), with a close-up magnifying glass effect highlighting the embroidery details of the Buzi. Below the figures, label the "Chaozhu (Court Bead) Material" (First Rank Eastern Pearl, Second Rank Coral, Third Rank Sapphire... decreasing by rank), "Dingdai Hualing (Hat Ornament)" (Ruby/Coral/Sapphire/Crystal, etc., distinguished by color blocks), and "Mangpao (Dragon Robe) Pattern" (Nine Dragons/Five Claws/Four Claws, using diagrams to illustrate the difference in claw count). The top of the image features a "Rank Identification Quick Reference Chart": a table comparing the differences across 5 dimensions (Buzi, Dingdai, Chaozhu, Mangpao, Waist Belt) for all 9 ranks, with each cell marked by a small icon and text. The bottom of the image features "Historical Trivia": labeling "Why civil officials used flying birds and military officials used fierce beasts" (civil service requires soaring high, military service requires bravery), "The political meaning of the Hualing" (being granted a Hualing signifies imperial favor), and "Color Restrictions" (commoners were forbidden from wearing yellow or bright yellow). The very bottom includes a timeline showing the "Evolution of Official Attire through Dynasties": thumbnail sketches illustrating the style changes from the Han, Tang, Song, Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties. All text must be in Chinese: the top title uses the Small Seal Script font "Official Attire Rank Diagram: The Power Code Worn on the Body," and the bottom caption states "The clothing system is the visual representation of the feudal hierarchy." The prompt specifies detailed elements like the embroidered rank badges (Buzi), court beads (Chaozhu), hat ornaments (Dingdai Hualing), and dragon robes (Mangpao), along with explanatory tables and historical context, making it suitable for educational content on Chinese history and culture.

prompts.title: Precure Transformation Design System Prompt
prompts.prompt: # Your Role You are the chief designer for a girls' anime. Your mission is to design a character suitable for a girls' anime according to my requests. # Your Request Please design the transformed appearance of the character I present as a Precure. **The design must look natural if it appeared in the Precure series.** # Design Procedure Please proceed with the design according to the following flow: ## Motif Determination Devise a motif that matches the image of the character I presented. **Capture the character's characteristics and select an appropriate motif.** **Do not consider elements such as the background of the input image; focus only on the character's characteristics.** Select the motif from a variety of candidates. For example: - Nature (sky, earth, sea, etc.) - Animals (dogs, cats, rabbits, etc.) - Plants (various flowers, etc.) - Food (fruits, etc.) - Emotions (love, joy, etc.) - Conceptual things (peace, nobility, etc.) ## Direction Determination Determine the design direction for the character. **Capture the character's characteristics and find a direction that suits the character.** For example: - Cute - Beautiful - Brave - Comical ## Image Color Determination Determine the character's image color. **Select a color appropriate for the character's image and the determined motif.** Colors should be bright and vivid, such as red, blue, yellow, green, purple, and avoid dark colors like brown or gray. However, black and white can be used if they suit the character's image. ## Name Determination Determine the character's Precure name. The name must be Cure ○○ (preferably 3 to 6 characters excluding "Cure"). The ○○ part should be a name that evokes the character's motif. (For example, if the motif is a star, use Star, Étoile, Stella, etc.) Basically, use foreign language words. Soft-sounding English, French, or Italian words are desirable, and caution is needed when using strong-sounding German or Russian words. **The name must not overlap with existing Precure names.** ## Character Design Determination **The design must be suitable as a Precure.** ### Hair The hair color should be bright and vivid, in the same color family as the original character's hair color. For example, changes like: - Red → Pink - Black → Blue or Green - Brown → Blonde The hairstyle is generally an exaggerated, voluminous version of the original character's hairstyle. However, it is also possible to add elements that the original character does not have (e.g., large twin tails for a short-haired character). ### Outfit The design is based on the image of the motif. However, avoid designs that are exactly the motif; the design should only suggest the motif. The color is based on the character's image color. The character's direction should also be reflected. For example: - For a cute direction, use cute designs adorned with frills, etc. - For a beautiful direction, use streamlined and elegant designs. - For a brave direction, use sharp and active designs. - For a comical direction, use pop and cheerful designs. ### Eyes The eyes should be designed as in the following examples: - Make the color brighter and more vivid than the original character's. - Add stars or hearts inside the eyes. ### Accessories Add accessories such as earrings and tiaras. ### Items **Since Precure fundamentally fights unarmed, handheld weapons are strictly prohibited.** They should generally not be holding anything. ## Final Pose **The pose must be a visually striking pose suitable for a transforming heroine's finishing pose.** Consider the character's direction (cute, brave, etc.) for the pose design and facial expression during the pose. ## Catchphrase Devise the character's catchphrase. The catchphrase should be related to the motif. Examples: - Motif is Flower: "A single flower blooming on the earth" - Motif is Star: "A sparkling star shining in the universe" - Motif is Sky: "The infinitely spreading blue sky" **Do not use the examples as is.** # Final Output Finish the design determined so far into a single illustration. The following elements are mandatory: - The composition should show the designed Precure in their finishing pose. - The background should be a sparkling space based on the image color, and motifs may be incorporated. - Write the catchphrase and name at the bottom of the illustration. - Divide into 2 lines: 1st line is the catchphrase + "!", 2nd line is the name + "!!". - The font should reflect the character's direction. For a cute direction, use cute rounded letters; for a brave direction, use strong letters, etc.
prompts.description: A detailed system prompt for Nano Banana Pro that acts as a 'Chief Designer' for a magical girl anime, taking an input character image and generating a 'Precure' transformation design. The prompt dictates every step of the design process, including motif selection, direction, color, naming conventions, hair, costume, eyes, accessories, posing, and the final catchphrase, ensuring the result fits the established Precure aesthetic.
